name: Session-Structuring Actions
description: Actions that organize each CBT session collaboratively, maintain focus, connect sessions over time, and translate discussion into between-session practice.

goal.objective: Create a predictable, collaborative, and clinically focused session structure.

success_levels.ideal: The agenda is jointly set, priority problems are addressed, progress and homework are reviewed, summaries support shared understanding, and the session ends with feedback and a clear new assignment.
success_levels.acceptable: Most structural elements are present, but one or more elements are brief, incomplete, or insufficiently collaborative.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The session is unstructured, therapist-dominated, disconnected from prior work, or ends without shared understanding and an actionable plan.

goal.reward_hint: The patient can state the agenda and key conclusions, participates in prioritization, and understands the agreed homework.

states: At the beginning of each session
When several problems compete for attention
At the end of each session
When continuity across sessions is weak

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Agenda Setting
micro_actions.description: Invite the patient to propose topics, add clinically relevant priorities, negotiate scope, and confirm a shared agenda.

micro_actions.name: Mood and Symptom Check-In
micro_actions.description: Briefly assess current mood, symptom change, important events, functioning, and any clinically relevant deterioration since the previous contact.
states: A change in presentation is observed

micro_actions.name: Review Previous Homework
micro_actions.description: Review whether the previous assignment was attempted, what happened, what was learned, and what barriers affected completion.

micro_actions.name: Prioritize One or Two Target Problems
micro_actions.description: Select one or two formulation-relevant problems that can be addressed meaningfully within the available session time.

micro_actions.name: Provide Periodic Summaries
micro_actions.description: Summarize key links, conclusions, and decisions during the session, then invite correction or additions from the patient.

micro_actions.name: Elicit End-of-Session Feedback
micro_actions.description: Ask what was useful, unclear, uncomfortable, or missing and use the response to improve subsequent work.

micro_actions.name: Assign New Homework
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively define a specific, feasible, formulation-linked task, including rationale, steps, timing, anticipated barriers, and how outcomes will be reviewed.
states: A hypothesis should be tested between sessions

name: Therapeutic Relationship Actions
description: Actions that strengthen collaboration, understanding, trust, and repair while preserving the patient's active role in treatment.

goal.objective: Maintain a collaborative therapeutic alliance characterized by agreement on goals, agreement on tasks, and a workable interpersonal bond.

success_levels.ideal: The patient feels heard and respected, openly contributes to goals and tasks, understands the work, provides feedback, and alliance strains are identified and repaired.
success_levels.acceptable: The relationship is adequate for treatment, but feedback, collaboration, or repair is inconsistent.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The patient feels misunderstood, pressured, excluded, or persistently disengaged, and relational strain is not addressed.

goal.reward_hint: The patient communicates openly, corrects misunderstandings, collaborates on decisions, and remains engaged after disagreements.

states: When distress or hesitation is expressed
When goals or tasks are negotiated
When misunderstanding, disagreement, withdrawal, or disengagement appears

micro_actions.name: Reflective Listening
micro_actions.description: Reflect the patient's meaning, emotion, and perspective accurately without prematurely interpreting or redirecting.

micro_actions.name: Empathic Validation
micro_actions.description: Communicate that the patient's emotional response is understandable in context without necessarily endorsing every interpretation or conclusion.
states: Distress, shame, fear, anger, or discouragement is expressed

micro_actions.name: Clarification
micro_actions.description: Ask focused, non-assumptive questions to resolve ambiguity and check the accuracy of the therapist's understanding.

micro_actions.name: Collaborative Goal Negotiation
micro_actions.description: Develop or revise treatment goals jointly so they remain meaningful to the patient and clinically coherent.

micro_actions.name: Check Patient Understanding
micro_actions.description: Ask the patient to explain key ideas, rationales, or plans in their own words and correct misunderstandings collaboratively.
states: Confusion or passive agreement is suspected

micro_actions.name: Elicit Patient Feedback
micro_actions.description: Invite direct feedback about the session, intervention, pace, fit, and therapeutic relationship.

micro_actions.name: Repair Alliance Ruptures
micro_actions.description: Name possible tension or withdrawal, invite the patient's perspective, acknowledge the therapist's contribution when relevant, and renegotiate goals or tasks.

name: Cognitive Interventions
description: Actions that help the patient identify and evaluate automatic thoughts, distortions, assumptions, and core beliefs through guided discovery rather than persuasion.

goal.objective: Increase cognitive awareness and flexibility while supporting the patient's own evidence-based conclusions.

success_levels.ideal: The patient identifies relevant cognitions, evaluates them with balanced evidence, develops credible alternatives, and can apply the process with increasing independence.
success_levels.acceptable: The patient participates and reaches partial insight or a tentative alternative with therapist support.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The intervention is leading, argumentative, disconnected from the formulation, or produces superficial agreement without patient discovery.

goal.reward_hint: The patient generates links, evidence, and balanced alternatives in their own words and reports a meaningful shift in conviction or emotion.

states: A triggering situation and emotional response have been identified
Automatic thoughts or beliefs appear linked to distress or behavior
A recurrent pattern requires deeper belief work
The patient is sufficiently regulated and willing to examine the cognition

micro_actions.name: Guided Socratic Questioning
micro_actions.description: Use open, curious, non-leading questions that help the patient examine meanings, assumptions, evidence, and alternatives.
states: The patient is able to reflect
micro_actions.delivery_requirement: Questions should facilitate patient discovery rather than steer the patient toward a predetermined answer.

micro_actions.name: Identify Automatic Thoughts
micro_actions.description: Elicit the specific words, images, or meanings that occurred in a triggering situation and connect them with emotion and behavior.
states: A recent problem event is discussed
Emotion intensified in a specific context

micro_actions.name: Identify Cognitive Distortions
micro_actions.description: Collaboratively identify recurring thinking patterns such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, or all-or-nothing thinking without using labels as criticism.

micro_actions.name: Examine Evidence For and Against Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Review concrete evidence supporting and contradicting a target cognition, including evidence quality and alternative explanations.
states: A target thought or belief is sufficiently clear

micro_actions.name: Generate Balanced Alternative Interpretations
micro_actions.description: Support the patient in constructing a realistic, personally credible interpretation that integrates the available evidence.
states: The initial interpretation appears incomplete or biased

micro_actions.name: Decatastrophizing
micro_actions.description: Explore the feared outcome, its probability, coping possibilities, and the most likely outcome to reduce catastrophic overestimation.
states: The patient can examine feared consequences safely

micro_actions.name: Downward-Arrow Technique
micro_actions.description: Use repeated meaning-focused questions to identify deeper assumptions or core beliefs underlying an automatic thought.
states: Deeper belief work is clinically indicated

micro_actions.name: Identify and Modify Intermediate Assumptions and Core Beliefs
micro_actions.description: Identify conditional rules, attitudes, assumptions, and core beliefs; evaluate their origins, current effects, evidence, and more adaptive alternatives.

name: Behavioral Interventions
description: Actions that change avoidance, inactivity, skill deficits, and maintaining contingencies through planned behavior and experiential learning.

goal.objective: Increase adaptive engagement, test formulation-based predictions, strengthen skills, and reduce behavior that maintains problems.

success_levels.ideal: The patient collaboratively completes well-specified behavioral tasks, reviews outcomes, learns from discrepancies, and generalizes useful behavior.
success_levels.acceptable: The patient attempts tasks with partial completion or learning, and barriers are reviewed constructively.
success_levels.unsuccessful: Tasks are imposed, poorly specified, unsafe, unrelated to the formulation, or not reviewed for learning.

goal.reward_hint: The patient completes or meaningfully attempts the task, compares prediction with outcome, and identifies transferable learning.

states: Avoidance, withdrawal, inactivity, or skill deficits maintain difficulties
A belief can be tested behaviorally
The patient is ready and the intervention is clinically appropriate

micro_actions.name: Behavioral Activation
micro_actions.description: Increase contact with meaningful, reinforcing, or mastery-related activities through graded, collaboratively selected action.
states: Low activity, withdrawal, or loss of reinforcement is present

micro_actions.name: Activity Scheduling
micro_actions.description: Plan specific activities by time and context, balance demands and restorative activities, and review mood, mastery, or learning afterward.

micro_actions.name: Behavioral Experiments
micro_actions.description: Define a testable prediction, design a safe and feasible experiment, specify observations, and compare expected with actual outcomes.
states: A belief has a behavioral prediction
Experiential evidence is likely to be informative

micro_actions.name: Problem Solving
micro_actions.description: Define the problem, generate options, evaluate consequences, select a feasible step, implement it, and review the result.
states: A practical barrier is maintaining distress
The patient feels stuck or overwhelmed

micro_actions.name: Graded Exposure or Exposure With Response Prevention
micro_actions.description: Develop a clinically appropriate hierarchy and conduct graded exposure, with response prevention when indicated, while monitoring learning, distress, and safety.
states: Phobia-related avoidance or an appropriate exposure target is present
A qualified clinician has determined exposure is indicated
micro_actions.safety_note: Real-time exposure or exposure with response prevention requires clinical judgment and must not be autonomously delivered by an AI system. A qualified clinician should lead or directly supervise the intervention.

micro_actions.name: Skills Practice
micro_actions.description: Teach, model, rehearse, and provide feedback on a formulation-relevant coping, communication, behavioral, or problem-solving skill.
states: Practice can improve functioning or treatment implementation

name: Cross-Cutting Delivery Competence and Clinical Oversight
description: Competence is evaluated by how an intervention is selected and delivered, not only by its nominal label. The same technique may be high-quality CBT when it supports discovery and collaboration, or poor CBT when it becomes leading, persuasive, rigid, or unsafe.

goal.objective: Ensure every intervention is formulation-guided, collaborative, appropriately paced, competently executed, and within safe clinical boundaries.

success_levels.ideal: The intervention is selected from the evolving formulation, delivered non-leadingly, adapted to patient response, checked for understanding, and escalated to human clinical judgment when required.
success_levels.acceptable: The intervention is broadly appropriate but contains minor problems in timing, pacing, collaboration, or follow-through.
success_levels.unsuccessful: The intervention is chosen from symptoms alone, delivered persuasively or mechanically, ignores patient response, or crosses a boundary requiring clinician oversight.

goal.reward_hint: The patient demonstrates authentic understanding or discovery, remains collaboratively engaged, and the intervention is adjusted when its effect differs from expectations.

states: When the patient's response differs from expectations
When disagreement, confusion, distress, or disengagement emerges
Whenever an intervention requires clinical judgment or direct risk management

micro_actions.name: Select Interventions From the Current Case Formulation
micro_actions.description: Choose the intervention based on the current links among triggers, thoughts, emotions, behaviors, physiological responses, beliefs, and maintaining factors rather than symptoms alone.

micro_actions.name: Facilitate Discovery Rather Than Persuasion
micro_actions.description: Use questions, summaries, and evidence review to help the patient reach their own conclusions instead of pressing for therapist-preferred answers.

micro_actions.name: Adapt Pacing and Intensity
micro_actions.description: Adjust complexity, emotional intensity, and task difficulty according to understanding, readiness, distress, and observed response.
states: The patient is overwhelmed, confused, or disengaged
A task is too easy or too difficult

micro_actions.name: Monitor Immediate Effect and Correct Course
micro_actions.description: Check understanding, emotional response, alliance impact, and learning during and after the intervention, then modify the approach when needed.
states: After an unexpected or negative response

micro_actions.name: Escalate to Qualified Human Clinical Oversight
micro_actions.description: Do not autonomously conduct interventions that require real-time clinical judgment, especially exposure-based procedures; limit AI use to clinician-approved support such as preparation, documentation, or review.
states: Exposure or response prevention is considered
Safety or clinical complexity exceeds autonomous system boundaries
